notes.decision: ϩⲣϥⲟⲣⲉ analyzed as a Lyc verbal noun built on Greek ϥⲟⲣⲉⲓ 'wear, bear' — 'comes-wearing/being-borne in the holy ones.' Translated 'comes to be worn in the holy ones' to preserve the indwelling-as-garment image (cf. ⲣⲫⲟⲣⲉ in accumulated vocab for the First Man wearing his Five Sons as armor).

Per accumulated glossary, ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲉⲥ = 'the Ancient One.' In this anthropological context (the Light-Mind binding the X within the body of flesh) the term clearly designates the Manichaean 'Old Man' (palaios anthrōpos) — the dark, fleshly self that the Light-Mind subdues and binds within the body. 'Ancient One' retained for terminological consistency, but the Pauline 'old man' resonance is intended.

Obscure form. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲉϣϣⲉ 'it is fitting/necessary,' or a frozen demonstrative-deictic 'behold.' Translated '[it stands fixed]' tentatively — the disciple is summarizing what follows from what the apostle taught.

Lexeme uncertain. Context (paired with the next line's 'unchanging, unmeasured great god' and 'how does he become confined in the smallness of the body') requires a noun for change/variation/alteration that the disciple observes phenomenologically in the saint, contrasting with the Light-Mind's intrinsic immutability. Tentatively 'alteration.' Possibly related to ⲡⲱϣⲥ 'split, divide' or to ⲃⲗ̄ⲥ̄ 'weakness/decay.'

Verbal lexeme of uncertain root, paralleling ⲛⲁⲧϣⲓⲃⲉ ⲛⲁⲧϣⲓ ('unchanging, unmeasured') as predicate of the Mind's incarnation. Context (within the smallness of the body) demands a verb of confinement/restriction. Translated 'be confined' — possibly Lyc reflex of a verb of narrowing or dwelling-in-tight-space.

ϩⲥⲁⲧϥ̄ analyzed as Lyc reflex of ϩⲁⲣⲁⲧϥ̄ / ϩⲁⲧⲏϥ 'beside him, near him.' The disciple's third question concerns the relational mode of the Mind's presence in/beside the holy person. Translated 'whose Mind is beside him.'

The transcription symbol ⳨ is a staurogram-like ligature standing for ϯ in this manuscript, confirmed by ⳨ⲟⲩ = ϯⲟⲩ 'five' (line 24), Ⲧⲙⲁϩ⳨ⲟⲩ = 'the fifth' (line 3), and ⳨ⲧⲱⲃ̄ϩ = ϯⲧⲱⲃϩ 'I beseech' (line 7). I have transcribed it as ϯ throughout the Coptic field.
Translated as 'if (truly)' — Lycopolitan reflex of ⲉϣϫⲉ 'if (it is the case that)', introducing the conditional protasis of the disciple's question.

Tentatively translated as 'great is' — likely a Lycopolitan qualitative form related to ⲛⲁⲁ/ⲛⲁϣⲉ 'be great/many'. The parallel structure 'ⲛⲁϯ X ... ⲛⲁϯ Y' (great is X, great is Y) fits the acclamatory rhetoric. Alternative readings (ⲛⲁ-ϯ 'will give' or particle) are possible but less contextually fitting.
Translated as 'the watcher' — from root ⲱⲣϫ/ⲱⲣϩ 'guard, watch, fasten' (cf. accumulated ⲁϩⲟⲩⲱⲣⲟⲩⲱⲣⲉϩ 'keep guard'). The construction 'watcher of those who watch' is an emphatic genitive-of-source.

Translated as 'the living spring' — ϩⲁⲗⲙⲉ likely Coptic ϩⲁⲗⲙⲉ/ⲍⲁⲗⲙⲉ 'spring, well, source.' Paired with ⲃⲉⲃⲉ 'gush forth' (in accumulated vocabulary, used cosmogonically of element-emergence), confirming hydrological-cosmological reading.

Translated 'those who thirst' — Lycopolitan ⲁⲃⲉ for ⲉⲓⲃⲉ/ⲱⲃⲉ 'thirst.' The collocation 'gushing forth in those who thirst, that they may drink and live' confirms gustatory-soteriological reading. Distinguished from the homophonous ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲟⲟⲩⲧ 'the dead.'

Translated tentatively as 'the seventh' — reading as ⲡⲙⲉϩ-ⲍ̄ where ⲭ is a Lycopolitan orthographic variant of ϩ and ϩ̄ (with supralinear bar) likely represents the numeral ⲍ̄ = 7. The cosmic body-mapping fits a 7-firmament cosmology. Alternative: 'eighth' if ϩ̄ = ⲏ̄ = 8.

Translated 'their neck' — ⲙⲟⲩⲧ has the body-part sense 'neck/sinew' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲧ 'sinew' in body-mapping context). Here in cosmic-anatomical sequence following 'head' (ⲧⲁⲡⲉ, line 22), 'neck' fits.

Translated tentatively as 'their shaft' — a body-part term in the cosmic-anatomical series after 'head' and 'neck.' Etymology unclear; possibly a variant for shoulder, spine, or neck-piece. Awaits parallels.
Translated 'their ribs' — Lycopolitan plural on ⲥⲡⲓⲣ 'rib' (Crum). Fits the cosmic-anatomical mapping where rib structures correspond to firmamental layers.

Translated 'their navel' — ϩⲁⲗⲡⲉ/ϩⲉⲗⲡⲉ 'navel.' The navel = sphere of stars in the cosmic-anatomical correspondence is a known Manichaean cosmological motif (the cosmic axis through the navel-of-the-world).
Translated 'four' — Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ (cf. accumulated ⲡⲩⲧⲟⲉ 'the four'). The 'four worlds' may refer to the cosmological quarters/climes.
Translated 'their thighs' — likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲕⲉϩⲥ 'loin/thigh' or ⲕⲏⲧ 'thigh.' Fits the descending body-mapping (after navel, before feet).
Translated 'their legs' — possibly Lycopolitan plural for legs/calves. Paired with ⲛⲉⲩⲟⲩⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'their feet' as a lower-body doublet at the bottom of the cosmic-anatomical sequence.
Translated 'zone' — likely Lycopolitan variant of ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ (Greek ζώνη), the cosmic girdle/zodiacal zone (in accumulated vocabulary). The ϩ/ⲍ alternation is regular in Lyc orthography.
Greek loanword ἧπαρ 'liver' with Lyc. ⲍ-onset and possessive prefix ⲡⲉϩ- 'his.' Standard organ-term; here mapped to the cattle (quadrupeds) in the macrocosmic body-schema.
Lyc. plural of ϩⲁⲗⲏⲧ 'birds' (cf. accumulated ⲛⲍⲛⲍⲁⲗⲗⲉⲧⲉ). Birds-in-air paired with fish-in-water and creeping things-on-earth as the canonical three creature-strata.
Lyc. for ⲛϫⲁⲧϥⲉ 'creeping things, reptiles' (with ⲝ for ϫ). The three creature-strata schema (cattle/birds/fish/reptiles) maps body-parts to the visible creation.
Read as 'his outer skin/hide' = ϣⲁⲁⲣ 'skin' in Lyc. orthography. The skin as the outer enclosing surface = ⲥⲁⲃⲧ 'wall' surrounding the cosmos with the great fire (Manichaean firmament-wall motif).
Translated 'the All' tentatively. The form is unusual; could be a Lyc. variant of ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ̄/ⲡⲧⲏⲣⲥ̄ ('the totality'). Confidence low.

Possibly 'his gall/bile' — semantic field of bitterness (cf. accumulated ⲥⲓϣⲉ 'bitterness'). The bile as bitter humor maps to darkness in the body-schema. Translation deliberately left in apparatus pending parallels.

Lyc. ⲙⲉⲍⲧⲉ = ⲙⲟⲥⲧⲉ 'hatred.' 'His great hatred' identified as the will/desire of some great cosmic principle. Affective interiority mapped onto cosmic geography — characteristic Manichaean correspondence.
ⲙⲟⲟⲙⲉ = 'vein, channel' (per accumulated vocab). His veins = the springs/waters of the cosmos. Direct correspondence: the body's water-channels ARE the cosmic water-channels.
Reading as 'they have given/positioned (in) the middle of the worlds' — ϯ 'give' here in the sense of 'placing.' The five gods are positioned at the cosmological mid-point.
ⲧⲏⲟ̄ likely qualitative 'sown/planted' or 'fastened' (cf. ⲧⲱϩⲉ); 'in him' = within the macrocosmic body. Translated 'established in him' for clarity. Confidence moderate.
Privative ⲛ̄ⲁⲧ- + verbal compound ⲁⲧ-ⲛⲕⲁⲧⲉ ('without sleeping' from ⲛⲕⲟⲧⲕ̄ 'sleep'). 'The Unsleeping (Watchers)' — standard Manichaean designation of the cosmic guardians who never close their eyes.

Greek κάτοχος 'holder, possessor, restrainer' with Lyc. relative ⲫⲉⲧ- prefix. Identifies the first faculty (Mind = ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ) with a cosmic Holder/Restrainer figure. Possibly the Mother of Life or a comparable Manichaean figure who holds back chaos. Retained as Greek term to preserve technical specificity.
'The great King of Honor' — standard Manichaean title (already in accumulated vocab). Here identified with the second faculty, Thought (ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ).
ⲑⲃ̄ⲟ = 'humble, abase, bring low' (per accumulated vocab); 3sg.m perfect ⲁϩ- prefix. Subject likely the King of Honor humbling something.

'Palamas of the Light' — identifies the third faculty, Teaching (ⲧⲥⲃⲱ), with this cosmic figure. Cf. accumulated ⲡⲁⲗⲁⲙⲁⲥ 'contriver, cunning craftsman' — but here a positive light-figure, perhaps the cosmic light-craftsman who fashions instruction.
'The King of Glory' — standard Manichaean cosmological figure (κατόχος of the seventh heaven in some traditions, or the Third Ambassador). Identified with the fourth faculty, Counsel (ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ).
Lyc. = ⲙⲛ̄ⲧϩⲁⲣϣ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'longsuffering, patience' (literally 'state of long-of-heart'). A virtue.
Greek ὠμοφόρος 'shoulder-bearer' — the cosmic Atlas/Pillar of Glory figure. Identified with the fifth faculty, Reflection (ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ). Note shift from plural ⲛⲱⲙⲟⲫⲟⲣⲟⲥ in earlier vocab.
'The lower side' (per accumulated vocab) — the wisdom that is below, contrasted with the Mind that is above (line 21). Spatial cosmological pairing.

Translated 'the Rising' from root ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise, stand up.' The five 'noetic ones of the Rising' parallel the cosmic Ascent — the upward-directional principle of the Manichaean light system. Alternative readings 'the Strife/Resurrection' possible but less anchored in immediate context.

'The seven sons of the First Man' — likely the Five Sons + Call (ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ) + Hearing (ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ) yielding seven, since the present passage explicitly counts 5 noetic + Call + Hearing = 7. ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡⲧ = ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ + nominalizing -ⲧ, taken as the standard 'First (Man)' (ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ).
Variant orthography of ⲡⲗⲓⲗⲟⲩ 'the Youth' — same Manichaean Christological epithet (cf. accumulated vocabulary). Possibly metathesis or Lycopolitan dialectal alternation.

Translated 'torpor' (state of sluggish neglect / oblivion-sleep) — recurs five times on this page in pairing with ⲕⲣⲁϥ 'guile' (lines 11, 15, 26, 31) and once in the sea (l.23 'great torpor'). Both contexts fit a Manichaean νωθρία/forgetfulness-sleep cast by matter. Etymology unclear; may relate to ⲃⲱϣ 'be ignorant/forget' or to a dialectal abstract for 'lapse.' Same translation maintained throughout for consistency.
Greek φερέκατοχος 'bearer/holder of the captives' — Manichaean technical figure functioning as warden of the bound powers. Retained in transliteration to preserve the technical title.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲉⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'the prison.' Confirmed by the immediately following ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲧⲙⲏⲣ 'of the bound ones' — standard Coptic carceral collocation. Distinct from ⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'destruction' that appears nearby (line 31).

Read as 'darkness/blackness' (variant of ⲱⲕⲙ̄ / Sah. ⲕⲁⲕⲉ-related). Phrase 'the entire darkness of Death' fits standard Manichaean cosmological idiom for the totality of the Dark Realm bound by the Pillar.
Verb root unidentified; editor's restoration ϣⲉ may indicate ⲧⲟⲩⲣⲁϣⲉ 'cause to rejoice' (improbable in context) or a verb of rousing/agitation. Translation left blank, flagged for parallel research.
Read as ⲁⲥⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄ 'she/it was molded/established' (with intrusive ⲣ), 3sg.f. perfect of ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄ 'shape, fashion' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲛ̄ⲕ 'formation'). Subject is matter/Hyle as cosmic mother.

Tentatively 'the labor' from ⲃⲱⲕⲉ/ⲃⲁⲕⲉ 'work, toil.' Could alternatively be 'the city' (ⲃⲁⲕⲓ) or 'the maidservant.' Context (third firmament, encampment of the Great King of Honor) underdetermined. Flagged for parallels.
Read as 'disturbance, agitation' from ⲟⲩⲱϣ-stem (cf. ⲟⲩⲱϣⲣ̄ 'disturb, scatter'). Pairs naturally with 'guile' and 'torpor' as the three traits arising in the Watchers' encampment.

Translated 'the irons' as the Watchers' revealed metallurgical secrets — direct echo of the Enochic tradition where the fallen Watchers teach humanity the working of iron and the mysteries of heaven. The pairing 'opened the irons / disclosed the mysteries' confirms the Enochic reception in Manichaean cosmography.

Lexeme of uncertain identity opening a new section after 'leer.' Possibly the feminine of ⲡⲁⲗⲁⲙⲁⲥ 'the contriver' (already in vocabulary), or a Greek-derived term (ταλαμᾶς?), or a proper name. Left transliterated as 'Talamas' pending parallels.

Translated 'strife' throughout the page (lines 1, 23, 30) for this recurring noun denoting the cosmic battle. The opening 'a strife arose' parallels Manichaean cosmogonic-historical narrative; ⲕⲣⲁϩ is paired with ⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ-class semantics. Etymology uncertain — possibly Lyc form related to a martial root; flagged in proposed_terms.
Read as feminine possessive ⲧⲉϩ- + ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲟⲗⲏ 'her encampment,' parallel to masculine ⲡⲉϩ- in glossary. Antecedent presumably continues from previous page — likely Hyle/Matter or the world.

Translated 'the chosen one' per accumulated vocabulary, though here the referent appears to be the encampment (= the earth/world?) rather than Zarathustra. The sense 'the elect (place)' may be intended.

Compound ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix) + ⲡⲁⲓⲥ. Translated 'place of battle' since the figure named is Adamas of Light, the cosmic warrior who battles the dark powers. ⲡⲁⲓⲥ here likely denotes combat/striking/contest. Etymology of ⲡⲁⲓⲥ uncertain; flagged in proposed_terms.
Translated 'the Great Counsel' per accumulated vocabulary entry. Here identified with the Great King of Glory and described as having authority over the three wheels (fire/wind/water).
Translated 'they sank' — Lycopolitan form likely from ⲗⲱⲕϩ̄ 'cast, throw, immerse.' Intransitive sense fits: the abortions are submerged/stuck in the three earths until the Ambassador's revelation.

Translated 'were laid open' — qualitative/perfect of an unidentified verb related to opening or stretching paths. Context (after the Ambassador reveals his image) requires path-opening semantics. Confidence low; flagged in proposed_terms.
Parsed as ⲧ-ⲟⲩ-ⲟⲓⲛ-ⲉⲓ 'their coming' (action-noun ⲟⲓⲛ- on ⲉⲓ 'come'), parallel to the formation ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ 'the dissolution' in vocab.
Singular 'the Omophoros' — distinct from plural ⲛⲱⲙⲟⲫⲟⲣⲟⲥ in vocab. Refers here to the chief Atlas-figure, also called Pillar of Glory.
Translated 'boundaries' tentatively from ⲧⲱϣ 'boundary, limit.' Lyc reflex with ⲱⲟ̄ⲥ for ⲱϣ.

Greek ἐγρήγοροι 'Watchers' — the fallen Watchers of 1 Enoch tradition, integrated into Manichaean cosmology as a class of fallen powers bound by the four angels in the prison of darkness. Their sons (the giants) are then expelled from the earth (line 28).
Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'prison.' The 'prison of the dark ones' = the eschatological-cosmic prison of the fallen Watchers.
'their sons' = the giants, sons of the Watchers and human women per 1 Enoch — expelled from the earth in the standard reception of the myth.
Translated 'he cast them downward' — ⲧⲁⲟ̄ⲥⲟⲩ likely from ⲧⲁⲩⲉ/ⲧⲁⲟⲩⲟ 'put forth, cast' with 3pl object suffix. Context: Jesus casting down the abortions at his revelation.

Translated 'the gathered earthquake' taking ⲥⲱⲱϩ as related to ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather' — a clustered/recurring seismic event. Alternative readings could include 'shaking' or 'rumbling.' The cosmic context indicates a specific structural earthquake at the third bone (third level/joint) of the Omophoros.
Translated 'barriers/bolts' tentatively — pairs naturally with ⲟⲩⲉⲛ 'open' in line 5 (one opens bolts/barriers). Could alternatively be 'channels' or 'passages.' Lexeme not securely identified.
Read as ⲟⲩ + ⲣ̄- + ⲱⲣϩ̄ ('to-watch/guard'): 'a watch, a watching-station' — Jesus 'took up a watch downward.' Fits cosmic-warden register where Jesus stands guard at threatened cosmic levels.
Read as 'for an hour/instant' — ⲉⲩⲥⲁ likely Lyc form of ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ 'hour, time-instant.' Recurs in line 9.
Translated 'courses' — likely plural of ⲥⲓⲟⲩ/ⲥⲓⲟⲟⲩ 'expanse, course' rather than 'stars.' Refers to the directional paths of wind, water, and fire elements.

'The lower bone of the Omophoros' — anatomical-cosmological reading: the Omophoros (cosmic Atlas) has bones/joints, and the lower one weakens/withers. The 'third bone' of line 1 is one such structural level.
Read as ϣⲁⲛⲧⲉϥ-ⲡⲱⲧⲥ̄ 'until he reaches' (ⲡⲱⲧⲥ̄ = Lyc reflex of 'reach, arrive at') with idiosyncratic infixed ϩ.
Translated 'to set them up' — possibly causative form of a setting/establishing verb. Tentative.
Read 'concerning him at the hour' (ⲁⲣⲁϩ = 'concerning him' [the Omophoros], ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲩ = 'at the hour'). The Apostle's discourse opens with the temporal frame of 'all the watches.'

Translated tentatively 'his magnitude/greatness' — ⲁⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲏⲏⲥ as abstract noun of greatness/extent. Etymology uncertain. Context (paired with 'small' and the 'rooted strong power') requires a magnitude-noun.

Translated 'the Old Man' here rather than glossary's 'the Ancient One.' In this corporeal-anthropological context (paired with Sin rooted in the body), the Pauline ὁ παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος ('old man') is the natural parallel — the unredeemed self mounted upon the body. Distinct from the cosmic Ancient One who reigns among doctrines (earlier vocab).
Translated 'tarries long in (his) rising' — ϩⲟⲩⲁⲥⲉ as Lyc reflex of ⲱⲥⲕ 'tarry, prolong'; ⲧⲟⲛⲱ = ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise.' Sin tarries long in arising even within great Wisdom — tenacious.

Translated 'his purpose of heart' — ⲛⲥⲏⲧ as Lyc variant of ⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'of heart'; same idiom as ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ in accumulated vocabulary. Mind of Light drives the body according to its (the Mind's) purpose of heart.
Translated 'casts' — ⲛⲏⲥⲥⲉ 'throw, cast' (Crum). Sin throws/casts disturbances into the body. Alternative: 'begets' (ⲙⲓⲥⲉ).

Translated 'the discernment and the wise-knowledge' tentatively. ⲥⲟⲩⲓⲧⲉ probably from the ⲥⲟⲟⲩⲛ 'know' family — 'discernment, sign, knowledge.' ⲥⲁⲏ from ⲥⲁϩ 'wise/teacher' — 'wise-knowledge' or 'teaching.' These are revealed to the powers of light. ⲥⲟⲩⲓⲧⲉ recurs in line 32 in the phrase 'verdict of cutting,' suggesting 'verdict/sentence/decree.'
Translated 'in due preparation' — ⲥⲉⲡⲧ from ⲥⲱⲡⲧ̄/ⲥⲃⲧⲉ 'prepare, fitness.' Pairs with 'established' (ⲥⲙⲁⲁⲛⲧ) as doublet for ordered, fitting action.
Read as ϣⲁⲩ-ϯ-ⲙⲁ 'they give place/consign' to enmity — judicial idiom 'consign over to enmity' = condemn. The powers of light deliver the rebellious to the punitive verdict.

Translated 'the verdict of cutting' — ⲥⲟⲩⲓⲧⲉ here functions as a punitive instrument/decree. ⲧⲟⲩ-ϯ = 'they give'; ϣⲱϩⲧ = ϣⲱⲱⲧ 'cut down, cut off.' The verdict authorizing the cutting (= execution/destruction).

Translated 'goodness' from Greek καλωσύνη (with prosthetic ⲁ-). Reading uncertain — letters dotted in transcription. Alternative ἀκακοσύνη 'innocence/guilelessness' is also possible if reading ⲁⲕⲁⲕⲟⲥⲩⲛⲏ. Either fits the moral-ascetic register.

Translated 'wearing' — ⲣ̄-ⲫⲟⲣⲉⲓ from Greek φορεῖν 'to wear, bear'; ⲛ- prefix forms a circumstantial 'as a wearer'. The Mind of Light dons the small body of flesh as a garment — standard Manichaean christological motif.

Translated 'is in oppression' — ⲫⲗⲓⲃⲉ from Greek θλίβειν 'press, afflict, oppress'. The cosmic gods stationed in the body are themselves 'in affliction' — the Manichaean motif of divine suffering for the sake of light-extraction. ⲟ̄ⲛⲟⲩ functions as locative-stative marker.

Provisionally rendered 'supports/foundations'. Lexeme not in standard Coptic dictionaries; the trees-with-roots image dominant in lines 6-8 suggests a noun denoting what holds something fast in place. Possibly cognate with ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'grasp, hold' (qualitative ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧ). Flagged for future parallel research.

Tentatively rendered '[reaching] upward' — the directional ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' is clear, but ⲉϩⲃⲓ̈ is uncertain. Possibly Lyc form of a verb of extension/reaching, or an adverbial of motion-up. The line continues into a lost portion of line 10.

Translated 'this Living Spirit' — Manichaean cosmological figure (the Great Architect/Builder), whose five sons bind the soul into the body. The 'his members' (ⲛⲉϩⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ) are the cosmic limbs through which he operates.

Translated 'Sin took this body forth'. ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ here is capitalized as the cosmic principle 'Sin' per terminology guide. The act parallels the cosmogonic seizure-of-body that follows in lines 14-17 where the Living Spirit re-establishes the body from the five dark bodies.

Translated 'the five Gods that are radiant' — ⲡⲣⲱⲩ qualitative of ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine, radiate'. Per correspondential principle, retained the active-emission verb-quality ('radiant' over 'shining' or 'bright'). The Five Sons of the Living Spirit are the radiant ones from whom the soul is taken forth before being bound in the body.

The five members of the body in correspondence with the five faculties: bone↔mind, sinew↔thought, vein↔teaching, flesh↔counsel, skin↔reflection. Each correspondence is a direct identity in the Manichaean register, not a comparison.
Translated 'foremost of the powers' — ⲙⲛⲧⲉϩⲧⲉ 'foremost rank' (from glossary) + ⲟ̄ⲁⲙ 'powers' (Lyc plural of ϫⲟⲙ). Refers to the Living Spirit's mind set at the head of the soul's faculties.

Tentatively translated 'they oppress the soul' — ⲭⲗⲟⲩⲱ unidentified, possibly Lyc reflex of ϫⲱⲗ 'twist, deceive, violate' or related to a constraint-verb. The context (the dark powers drawing the soul to evil works) requires a negative-action verb on the soul. Confidence low; flagged for parallel research.

Translated 'the practice that stands fast' — ⲙⲛⲧⲟⲁⲟⲩⲁⲛ from glossary ('practice/comportment') + qualitative ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲥ̄ 'stands fast'. Refers to the established/instituted practice of idol-worship to which the souls are humbled.

Tentatively rendered 'they make use' — ⲟ̄ⲁⲭⲏ may be Greek ἀρχή 'rule, beginning, principle' with ⲣ̄- 'do'. Could mean 'exercise rule/practice' but reading uncertain. Context: serving the beasts/animals (zoolatry) follows.
Rendered as 'mingled' — Lycopolitan qualitative likely from ⲱⲧⲉ/ⲧⲱϩ 'mix, mingle.' Fits the triadic series 'defiled, heaped together, mingled' describing Sin's confused forms.
Greek φορεῖν 'wear, bear (clothing)' — rendered 'donned' to capture the sense of Sin putting on Error and Forgetfulness as garments.
Lycopolitan ⲃⲱⲉ = Sah. ⲃϣⲉ 'forgetfulness'; capitalized as cosmic principle paired with Error (ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ).
ⲣ̄-ⲡⲱⲃⲱ 'do/make forgetting' = 'forget'. The triad substance/kind/manner echoes the established vocabulary triad (ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ + ⲅⲉⲛⲟⲥ + ⲣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ).
Rendered 'dwelling-place' — Lycopolitan compound ⲙⲁ-ⲛ̄- + verbal element from ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'dwell, settle.' The 'door of his dwelling' is the way back to the Father.

The structural pattern lines 13-21 follows: ϣⲁϩⲧⲟⲩⲱ (he raises) + faculty + ⲛϩⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (releasing it from) + body-part; then ⲛ̄ϩⲙⲟⲩⲣ (and binds) + Sin's counterpart-faculty in the body-part. Five faculties paired with five body-parts: mind/bone, thought/sinew, teaching/vein, counsel/flesh, reflection/skin.
Rendered 'sinew' (Sah. ⲙⲟⲩⲧ); paired with ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'thought' as the second faculty/body-part pair.
Rendered 'vein' — Coptic ⲙⲟⲩⲙⲉ 'vein, channel.' Paired with ⲧⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching' as third faculty/body-part pair.
Rendered 'skin' (Sah. ϣⲁⲁⲣ); paired with ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ 'reflection' as fifth faculty/body-part pair.
Lycopolitan ⲧⲍⲉ = Sah. ⲧϩⲉ 'manner, way.' Standard summary formula: 'This is the manner in which...'
Conjunctive 'and they (become) free' — ⲣⲙ̄ⲍⲉ = freeman/free (per accumulated vocabulary). The soul's faculties are made free from Sin's parallel members.
Imperfect with qualitative ⲃⲏⲩ from ⲃⲱⲕ 'go' = 'which had gone forth' — referring to Sin's five members that had emerged into the body.
'New Man' — ⲣⲙ̄ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ = 'man of newness'; the regenerated soul-construct fashioned by the Savior. Standard Manichaean technical term.
ⲡⲛⲉⲩ = ⲡⲛⲁⲩ 'the hour'; ⲁⲉ = δέ. Temporal connector: 'And the hour in which he will mold and fashion and refine the New Man, then he brings forth...'
Identifying gloss: the mind = love (ἀγάπη). Begins the explicit mapping of the five faculties to five virtues placed in the New Man (mind=love, thought=faith, teaching=perfection).
Lycopolitan ⲛⲁⲍⲧⲉ = Sah. ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'faith.' Maps to the second faculty (thought).
Reading 'the teaching' — ⲧⲉϩ likely a Lycopolitan article variant, or fem possessive ⲧⲉϥ→ⲧⲉϩ. Following the pattern, teaching is the third faculty mapped to ⲡⲭⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'perfection/completion.'

Translated 'the New Man' (Pauline καινὸς ἄνθρωπος). Analysis: ⲣⲙ̄- ('man of') + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ (Lyc. for ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'new'). Confirmed by antithesis with ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲉⲥ in line 15 = 'the Old Man' (παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος). The kephalaion is structured around this Pauline-Manichaean anthropological dyad: the New Man's five faculties produce virtues; the Old Man's same faculties are corrupted by Sin. NOTE: this corrects the accumulated-vocab gloss of ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲉⲥ as 'the Ancient One' for this context — here it is the Pauline 'old man.'

Translated 'the Old Man' (παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος, Pauline anthropology). The accumulated vocabulary glossed this as 'the Ancient One' from a different cosmological context. Here, the strict antithesis with ⲡⲣⲙ̄ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ ('the New Man') and the description of being 'bound' in lust, foolishness, and the spirit of darkness (lines 15-19) confirm the anthropological-soteriological reading: this is the unredeemed pre-conversion self, whose five faculties are corrupted.

Translated 'is mingled inward.' Most likely a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲱⲧ qualitative ⲧⲏⲧ 'be joined/mingled' with prosthetic/intensive ⲁ-. Recurs in line 24 of Sin mingled inward with the Mind of Light. Captures the Manichaean cosmological-anthropological motif of dark and light substances commingled within the body.

ϣⲁϩ- = Lycopolitan habitual ϣⲁϥ- 'he is wont to.' Translated as 'he places' / 'he purifies' for English fluency, though the habitual aspect is implied throughout the description of the New Man's regular practice.

Translated 'salt' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ; ϩⲙⲟⲩ = salt). Read alongside the preceding 'bitter words' as a gustatory-correspondence pair describing the corrupted speech of the Old Man under Sin's influence. Alternative reading 'blessing' (ⲥⲙⲟⲩ with ⲥ→ⲍ) is possible but less phonetically regular.
Translated 'time' (occasion). Standard Coptic ⲥⲁⲡ/ⲥⲏⲩ. The construction ⲟⲩⲛ ⲥⲁⲡ ⲉϣⲁⲣⲉ X = 'there is a time when X' introduces a habitual scenario.

Translated 'the separation — out of his hand.' ⲡⲧⲱⲣϫ̄ = 'separation, division' (Sah. ⲡⲱⲣϫ̄). ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲟⲧϩ̄ = 'from his hand' = 'from him.' The phrase signals Sin's act of severing the man from truth, throwing him into double-mindedness (ⲙⲛⲧϩⲏⲧⲥⲛⲉⲩ).

Translated 'this is the manner.' Likely a Lycopolitan demonstrative-form of ⲧⲛⲟ/ⲡⲛⲟ 'manner, way' (in accumulated vocabulary). Functions as the resumptive 'this manner' formula introducing the summary clause.
Greek ἐπεί 'since, when' — opens the chapter as a conditional/temporal protasis. The whole opening describes the consequence-chain when wisdom withdraws.
Read as ⲥⲓⲛⲉ 'pass, depart' + ⲁ-ⲧⲉⲥ-ⲙⲁ 'unto her place.' Wisdom (fem.) departs from the brother to her own place — the standard Manichaean motif of light-faculties withdrawing when sin enters.
Lyc. ϩⲱⲣⲃ̄ 'lurk, lie hidden, be slowed.' Translated 'has lurked-hidden' — Wisdom's withdrawal becomes a state of concealed inactivity rather than total disappearance.
Final word of L1 unclear; tentatively 'behold(?)' from Coptic ⲉⲓⲉ 'well, lo.' Could continue into the lacuna-start of L2. Flagged for parallels.
Lyc. ⲙⲛⲧϩⲁⲣϣϩⲏⲧ 'patience, longsuffering' (lit. 'state of slow-heartedness'). Standard Coptic virtue-noun.
Read as ⲁ-ϫⲱϩ 'unto strife, vexation' (Sah. ϫⲱϩ 'touch, strike, vex'). Lyc. ⲭ for ϫ is regular. Fits the conflict-progression of the kephalaion.

Translated 'multitude'; Lyc. ⲁϣⲁⲓ 'be many, multiply,' substantivized. Could alternatively be 'half/half-portion.' The collocation 'smallness of heart and multitude of sin' fits standard moral diagnosis.

Translated 'foolishness' (= Sah. ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲟϭ/ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲟⲃⲉ). The opposition with ⲥⲩⲙⲃⲟⲩⲗⲓⲁ ('counsel') and ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ('Mind of Light'), combined with the result 'becomes a fight and war,' confirms the negative valence. NOT to be confused with ⲥⲃⲱ 'teaching.'

Tentatively 'his threshing-floor' — Greek ἅλων (Coptic ϩⲁⲗⲱⲛ) with ⲣ for ⲗ. The threshing-floor is the standard Manichaean ecclesiological image for the gathered community where grain is separated. Alternative readings: 'his enclosure/company.' Confidence low.
Greek φορεῖν 'wear, bear (as garment).' Per accumulated vocabulary. Here used metaphorically: they 'wear' lust, slackness, haughtiness — vices as garments donned by the apostate brother.
Greek χαῦνος 'slack, loose, vain.' Translated 'slackness' — moral remissness, the opposite of patience.
Lyc. ⲙⲛⲧϫⲁⲥⲓϩⲏⲧ 'high-of-heart' = haughtiness, arrogance (cf. accumulated ⲝⲁⲥⲓϩⲏⲧ). Completes the vice-triplet lust/slackness/haughtiness.
Lyc. ⲟⲩⲁⲁⲧ-ϥ̄ 'alone, by himself.' The repeated emphasis 'alone' (lines 19, 20, 21) marks the apostate's isolation as the diagnostic sign of foolishness — anti-communal individualism.
ⲣⲙ̄- ('person of') + ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ('one, single') = 'of a single sort.' The brother eats/drinks 'of a single kind' — refusing communal sharing of varied food.

Tentatively 'exhortation' from ⲧⲱⲃⲥ̄ 'urge, exhort, persuade.' Alternative 'embrace, kiss' (from ⲧⲁⲡ 'embrace'). The community-restorative sense fits 'the X of the brothers does not please him' — what fellow-brothers offer that the apostate now rejects.
ⲣ̄-ϩⲛⲁ-ϥ 'be pleasing to him' — standard Coptic 'please.' Negated by ⲙⲁⲡⲉ.

Greek ἐνθύμησις 'thought, deliberation' + 'of death.' In the five-faculty system ⲉⲛⲑⲩⲙⲏⲥⲓⲥ corresponds to ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ 'counsel.' Here Sin lifts a death-counsel up to the brother's thought (ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ, 2nd faculty) — corruption rises through the faculties.
Tentatively 'in him' (= ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ⸗ⲉ̄ with unusual feminine/contracted suffix). Could be a relative form. Confidence low.
ⲥⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'fame, report, repute.' 'His fame is scattered in the church' — public knowledge of his apostasy spreads. Alternative 'his beauty' (ⲥⲁⲉⲓⲉ) less apt to context.
'The teachers of the church' (ⲥⲁⲃⲉⲩⲉ pl. of ⲥⲁϩ 'teacher'). The ecclesiastical office that intervenes for restoration — paralleling the apostolic ⲥⲁⲍ figure throughout the Kephalaia.

'The building of God' = the church as edifice. Pauline-Manichaean ecclesiological image; the goal of restoration is reincorporation into the divine architecture (cf. line 3 ⲡⲕⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉϩⲥⲛⲏⲩ 'the building-up of his brothers').

Lyc. ⲃⲱⲗⲕ 'be vexed, be angry,' substantivized as 'his vexation/anger.' The brother is rescued from his agitated/wrathful state through the brothers' counsel. Alternative 'his lack/poverty' (ⲃⲱⲱⲕⲉ) possible.

Translated 'the Five Vigils.' Parsed as ⲛ̄-ϯⲟⲩ-ⲣ̄ⲱⲉ where ⲣ̄ⲱⲉ is Lyc. for ⲣⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'wakefulness, vigil' (cf. ⲣ̄-ⲣⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'keep watch'). The disciplinary 'five watches' the teacher must establish. Cf. line 22 ⲛⲓⲁⲛⲟⲩⲣ̄ⲱⲉ 'the Watchers/Wakeful Ones,' which uses the same root cosmologically.
Translated 'leaps up.' Parsed as ⲱⲁ-ϥ-ϩⲉⲗ habitual + verb ϩⲱⲗ 'fly, leap' (cf. parallel ⲱⲁϩⲱⲧⲁⲣⲧⲣ̄ 'habitually disturbs' in next line). The subject is the disturbance/burdening that follows.

Translated 'the burdening of his mind.' ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ from Greek φορεῖν 'bear, wear, carry' (cf. ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲥ in glossary); nominalized: 'the bearing/burden.' The phrase parallels and is in apposition with ⲛ̄ϩⲱⲧⲁⲣⲧⲣ̄ 'disturbance.'

Translated 'his master.' ⲥⲁϩ = 'master, scribe, teacher'; here distinguished from ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ ('teacher') in the immediately following line, indicating a doublet 'master and teacher' for the apostle/instructor relation.

Translated 'before him.' Lyc. ⲛⲁϩⲣⲉϥ — preposition 'in the presence of him.' Functions to introduce the list of those 'before him' who become enemies (line 8 closes the inclusio with the same ⲛⲁⲍⲣⲉϩ).
Translated 'they become as enemies.' ⲱⲁⲩⲣ̄ = habitual + ⲣ̄- 'do/become'; ⲧⲍⲉ = ⲧ-ϩⲉ 'the manner of'; ⲛⲓⲝⲁⲝⲉ = ⲛⲓϫⲁϫⲉ 'the enemies.' Literally 'they become the manner of enemies.'

Translated 'arise away from his hand.' ⲡⲧⲱⲛⲉ = nominalized ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise, depart'; the love and desire 'depart from his hand,' i.e. leave his possession. Same root verb appears at line 16 'depart on a journey.'

Translated 'the part separated forth.' ⲡⲁⲥⲉ = Lyc. ⲡⲁϣ 'half, division, portion'; ⲡⲱⲣⲝ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'separate forth' (= ⲡⲱⲣϫ in vocab). The fallen man becomes a vessel of the schism/separation from the Church.

Translated 'he is filled instead by the evil spirit.' ⲍⲁ = Lyc. ϩⲁ 'under, by, instead of'; with the agentive sense 'is filled by/under (the influence of).' ⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲍⲁⲩ = 'the evil spirit' (cf. ϩⲟⲟⲩ/ⲍⲁⲩ in glossary).
Translated 'they fall.' Conjunctive ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ- + ⲉⲓⲣⲉ ⲛ-ϩⲉ or ⲣ̄-ϩⲉ — possibly 'do a fall' = 'fall' (ϩⲉ 'fall'). Subject is the evil spirits/error-powers who fall upon the disturbed teacher.
Translated 'in the flight of a bird.' ⲣ̄ⲫⲉ tentatively a verbal noun on ⲡⲏⲧ/ⲡⲱⲧ 'flee, fly' (Lyc. ⲡ→ⲫ regular). The simile compares disturbed cosmic men to migratory birds drawn far away.
Translated 'as foreigners.' Parsed as ⲛ-ⲟⲩ-ⲣ̄-ⲣⲁⲙⲛⲕⲁⲍ 'of becoming/being foreigners' or simply ⲛ-ⲣⲙⲛⲕⲁⲍ 'of strangers/of those who belong to a (foreign) land.' Cf. ⲣⲙⲛⲕⲁⲍ in glossary.
Translated 'I have made you see.' Idiomatic 'open your eye(s) forth' = reveal/make to see. ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ-ⲉⲓⲁⲧ⸗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ is the standard Coptic causative-revelation idiom.

Translated 'the matter.' ⲡⲱⲓ = 'that which belongs to'; ⲡⲍⲱϩ ambiguously could be ⲡϩⲱⲃ 'the work/matter' (cf. ⲡⲍⲱⲃ in glossary) or ⲡϩⲟ 'the face' or a possessive form. 'The matter' (= the bodily/cosmic structure they have shrunk into) fits the parallel with ⲥⲱⲙⲁ in line 29.

Translated 'lofty ... bent down.' ϩⲝⲁⲥⲉ = ϫⲁⲥⲉ 'lofty, high' (qualitative); ⲁϩⲕⲁⲗⲉⲝ probably ⲁϥ-ⲕⲱⲗϫ 'he bent (himself) down' — preserving the spatial-vertical contrast with the preceding 'great and high.'
Translated 'they are gathered.' Likely Lyc. qualitative of ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather, assemble.' The Watchers in the Zone are gathered/concentrated in their proper station.

Translated 'they are not defiled.' ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ 'defile, pollute'; with negative ⲉⲛ. The Watchers, though constrained in the Zone, remain pure — paralleling the Mind of Light's preservation despite bodily contraction.
Translated 'secrecy' from root ϫⲱⲡ/ⲭⲱⲡ 'be hidden, secret.' Paired here antithetically with ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ 'shame' as the two negative conditions of the Mind of Light when bound in the body.

Translated 'array/encampment' from Greek παρεμβολή (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲟⲗⲏ, ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲟⲗⲁⲩⲉ). The orthography ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲧⲟⲗⲏ may reflect scribal variation or metathesis. Alternatively could be παράπτωμα 'transgression,' but the body-falls-at-his-encampment imagery fits the established Manichaean martial-cosmological register.

Translated 'snares' tentatively. ⲥⲉⲕ may be Lyc. variant of ⲥⲱⲕ 'draw, drag, pull' as nomen actionis = 'pulls/draggings/snares' of Sin. Alternative: a corruption of ⲛⲕⲟⲧⲕ 'sleep' (sleep of Sin = Manichaean motif). Etymology uncertain.

Read as 3pl impersonal forms with ϩ- onset (Lyc. for ⲥⲉ-): 'they constrain/scatter/set them.' The triple verbal sequence describes how the dark powers handle the bound reflections of the body. Alternative reading as qualitatives ('constrained, scattered, set') is also possible.
Translated 'surpassing even more abundantly': ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ from ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄ 'pass over, exceed' + ⲉϩⲡⲍⲟⲩⲟ comparative 'unto the more.' Standard intensification idiom.

Translated 'is upon him' tentatively. ϩⲉⲓⲡⲉ is unidentified — possibly ϩⲉⲡ/ϩⲏⲡⲉ 'necessity, what is fixed,' or related to ϩⲓ-ⲡⲉ 'upon, over.' The general sense (something further weighs on him) fits context of describing additional impositions on the bound Mind.

Translated 'to defile' from ϫⲱϩⲙ̄/ϫⲱϩ 'pollute, defile.' Alternative reading as 'unto completion' (ⲁ + ϫⲱⲕ) is possible per accumulated vocabulary, but defilement of the elect by the false spirit fits Manichaean theology better here.
Per accumulated vocabulary, translated 'the Half' as cosmological designation of an intermediate region. Above 'all the works of the Half' = the realm beyond the manifest cosmos.
Translated 'they keep watch' — habitual ϣⲁⲩ + ⲣ̄- + ⲟⲩⲱⲣϩ. The root ⲟⲩⲱⲣϩ may be Lyc. for ⲱⲣϩ̄/ⲱⲣⲍ 'watch, guard, be settled.' Alternative: 'they are established/abide in.'
Translated 'his heart agrees': ⲡⲧⲱⲧ understood as 'persuaded, joined' from ⲧⲱⲧ 'agree, be joined,' here as predicate of ⲡⲉϩⲍⲏⲧ 'his heart' in habitual construction with ϣⲁⲣⲉ.
Translated 'itself/very' (intensive); per accumulated vocabulary ⲍⲱⲱϩ = ϩⲱⲱϥ 'himself/itself' as reflexive/intensive pronoun.

Translated 'the wonder.' The + symbol likely represents either ⲡ (article) giving ⲡϣⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'the wonder/marvel' or ϯ giving ϯ-ϣⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'I marvel/give wonder.' Read as articulated noun in object position of ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲧⲕ 'make known to you.'

Translated 'multitude' tentatively. The compound is unusual — possibly ⲙⲛⲧ- (abstract) + ⲗⲏⲙⲏϣⲉ/ⲣⲉⲙⲙⲏϣⲉ 'multitudinous person' = 'state-of-being-a-multitude.' Mani's 'multitude' would be his community/church. Alternative: 'manifoldness' or 'mass.'
Translated 'single shepherd' (μανϫϣⲱⲥ = ⲙⲁⲛⲉ-ⲉⲥⲟⲟⲩ 'shepherd of sheep'; ⲛⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'single, alone'). Mani's standard self-designation as the unique pastor of his church.
Translated 'silver' (Lyc. ⲍⲉⲧ = Sah. ϩⲁⲧ 'silver'), in standard metals enumeration with gold and bronze.

Translated 'violence' tentatively. May represent Greek βίας 'force, violence' with prosthetic ⲫ-, or be related to Coptic ⲑⲃⲓⲟ/ⲫⲃⲓⲟ 'humbling.' The contrast with line 31 ⲡⲟⲩⲫⲃⲓ̈ⲟ 'they did not subdue' suggests a coercive-force semantic field.
Translated 'they bind it' tentatively, from ⲙⲟⲩⲣ 'bind' with 3sg.f. suffix. The cosmos is 'bound' (subjugated) by means of favors and gifts. Alternative: μόρος 'fate' (Greek). Confidence low.
Translated 'they did not subdue' — negated perfect ⲙⲡⲟⲩ- + ⲫⲃⲓⲟ/ⲑⲃⲓⲟ 'humble, abase, subdue.' The kings of the cosmos with all their wealth and force did not actually conquer.

Translated 'far away in the speech of God' — circumstantial clause with ⲍⲙ̄ ('in') as instrumental/locative. The peoples are far in language and geography, yet bless Mani's name in all lands. Possibly read as 'far (yet) by the word of God' — i.e., the divine word reaches them in their distance.

Read as Coptic idiom for 'act beforehand against me' — ⲣ̄ + ⲡⲁⲧ-ⲟⲧⲟⲩ ('lay-foot/hand-against-them') with ⲛⲉⲙⲏⲓ̈ 'with me' (= 'against me' in hostile context). The kings together with magnates, orders, and powers attempted to cut Mani off from the truth but failed — Manichaean martyrological topos.

Read ⲁ̄ⲡⲉⲓ̈ as exclamatory 'Look! Behold!' and ⲉⲥⲭⲉ as Lyc. ⲉϣϫⲉ 'if/since.' The full sense: 'Look! — if then I am alone, why have they not been able against me?' The implied answer is that Jesus son of Greatness stands with him.

Lyc. ordinal ⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ 'third' (cf. ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ 'Third Ambassador'). The page presents a numbered list of Mani's distinctive achievements; matters one and two appeared on the previous page or are encompassed in lines 1-7.

Difficult form. Translated functionally as 'not one was found / could be a companion' — likely a Lyc. negative existential ⲛⲉⲩ-ⲕ̄ⲃⲛ̄ 'they were not equal/matched,' from ⲕⲱⲃ 'be paired, double.' The parallel construction in line 16 (ⲙ̄ⲡⲉ ⲟⲩⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ϣⲃⲣⲟ ⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ 'no single man has been companion to me') confirms the sense.
Unidentified term, possibly 'of (the host of) Sabaoth,' or a corrupt/obscure Lyc. word. Left tentative; flagged in proposed terms.

Translated 'great psalms of Wisdom' tentatively. ⲍⲁⲗⲙⲉ likely from Greek ψαλμοί 'psalms' with Lyc. ⲍ-onset; in the context of Mani's gifts to his Sons (the Manichaean elect), 'psalms of Wisdom' fits the documented Manichaean liturgical-instructional tradition. Alternative: ⲍⲁⲗⲙⲉ from ϩⲱⲗⲙ 'image, form' (cf. Hebrew ṣelem) — 'great forms of Wisdom.'

Qualitative modifying †ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ 'this generation.' Translated 'this latter (generation),' reading ⲭⲁⲃⲁⲁⲧ as related to ⲕⲱ 'leave behind' or ⲕⲁⲃ-ⲏⲏⲧ 'lowly, humble.' The contrast with the 'first apostles' supports a temporal-final sense ('the latter generation in which I am, contrasted with the apostolic ages of old').

Tentatively 'none of them either' — possibly ⲗ̄-ⲗⲁⲩⲉ-ⲍⲱⲥ-ⲁⲛ 'no one likewise either' or ⲗ̄ⲗⲟⲩ-ⲍⲱⲥ ⲁⲛ. Functions as emphatic negation reinforcing 'all the apostles did not do as I have done — none of them either.'
Rendered 'answered' as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ̄ 'answer, respond' (cf. ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'the answering' in glossary). The expected pattern is 'they answered and said to him.'

Translated 'grasp you in recompense for the favor.' ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ = 'grasp, hold,' ⲧⲱⲃⲓⲱ = 'recompense, requital.' The disciples acknowledge they themselves cannot fully repay the apostle — only the One who sent him can.
Rendered 'reach us / come to us' from ⲡⲱϩ 'reach, attain' + ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧⲛ̄ 'to our hand.' Literally 'has reached unto our hand.'
